In World Code, use the player ID a callback is given instead.\n\n## Make the player jump\n\nSets the player\'s velocity straight up, whatever they were doing.\n\n```js\napi.setVelocity(myId, 0, 9, 0)\n```\n\n## Push the player\n\nAdds to the player\'s velocity, so the push carries on from how they were already moving.\n\n```js\napi.applyImpulse(myId, 9, 0, 9)\n```\n\n## Teleport the player onto this block\n\n`thisPos` is the position of the code block or board that is running.\n\n```js\napi.setPosition(myId, thisPos[0] + 0.5, thisPos[1] + 1, thisPos[2] + 0.5)\n```\n\n## Send yourself a coloured message\n\n```js\napi.sendMessage(myId, "Welcome to my world!", { color: "orange" })\n```\n\n## Send a message to everyone\n\n```js\napi.broadcastMessage("The game starts in 10 seconds!", { color: "red" })\n```\n\n## Show flying text\n\nText that flies across the middle of the player\'s screen. The last number is how far away whatever caused it is, which sets how the text flies.\n\n```js\napi.sendFlyingMiddleMessage(myId, ["You found the secret room!"], 100)\n```\n\n## Say a line of dialogue\n\nShows a line below the crosshair, revealed word by word in a voice, with the speaker\'s name above it. It stays up until you hide it with `api.setClientOption(myId, "dialogue", null)`. In World Code, `sayDialogue` from `@plugins/dialogue` hides it for you after a while.\n\n```js\napi.setClientOption(myId, "dialogue", { line: "Welcome to my world!", speakerName: "Guide", voice: "regular" })\n```\n\n## Set the player\'s health\n\nLogs the health they had before.\n\n```js\nconst oldHealth = api.getHealth(myId)\napi.setHealth(myId, 50)\napi.log("Old health:", oldHealth)\n```\n\n## Give the player an item\n\n```js\napi.giveItem(myId, "Diamond Sword", 1)\n```\n\n## Place a block above this block\n\n```js\napi.setBlock(thisPos[0], thisPos[1] + 1, thisPos[2], "Block of Gold")\n```\n\n## Give the player a speed boost\n\nAn inbuilt effect, for 10 seconds.\n\n```js\napi.applyEffect(myId, "Speed", 10000, { inbuiltLevel: 1 })\n```\n\n## Make the player faster\n\nClient options change how the game behaves for one player.\n\n```js\napi.setClientOption(myId, "speedMultiplier", 2)\n```\n\n## Play a sound\n\n```js\napi.playSound(myId, "equip_leather1", 1, 1)\n```\n\n## Find every other player\n\nA function assigned without `const` or `let` stays defined for later code blocks, until World Code is next saved or the world restarts.\n\n```js\ngetOtherIds = () => {\n\tconst otherIds = []\n\tfor (const id of api.getPlayerIds()) {\n\t\tif (id !== myId) {\n\t\t\totherIds.push(id)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\treturn otherIds\n}\n```\n\n## Turn the other players into zombies\n\nUses `getOtherIds` from the snippet above.\n\n```js\nfor (const otherId of getOtherIds()) {\n\tapi.setPlayerPose(otherId, "zombie")\n\tapi.changePlayerIntoSkin(otherId, "head", "zombie")\n}\n```\n\n## Make everyone a floating wizard\n\n```js\nfor (const playerId of api.getPlayerIds()) {\n\tapi.setPlayerPose(playerId, "driving")\n\tapi.changePlayerIntoSkin(playerId, "head", "wizard")\n}\n```\n\n## Welcome players as they join\n\nWorld Code: `onPlayerJoin` runs each time a player joins, with their ID.\n\n```js\nonPlayerJoin = (playerId) => {\n\tapi.sendMessage(playerId, "Welcome! Type in chat if you need help.", { color: "green" })\n}\n```\n\n## Run code every second\n\nWorld Code: `tick` runs many times a second, and is given the time since the last one, in milliseconds.\n\n```js\nlet sinceLastSecond = 0\ntick = (ms) => {\n\tsinceLastSecond += ms\n\tif (sinceLastSecond >= 1000) {\n\t\tsinceLastSecond -= 1000\n\t\tapi.broadcastMessage("Another second has passed")\n\t}\n}\n```';

-        howItPlays: 'With buildCourse (the default) the game builds its own course on the first join: a line of platforms going east from startPosition (or, with courseShape "tower", a climb spiralling up around startPosition, a block higher every jump) in `stages` stages of `jumpsPerStage` jumps, a checkpointBlock pad at the start of each stage and the finishBlock at the end. Stage 1 is easy (1-block gaps, flat, wide platforms); every stage after has bigger gaps, small rises and drops and narrower platforms, never a jump a player can\'t make. With buildCourse false it uses a course the creator built. Players start at startPosition and race to a finishBlock. Standing on a checkpointBlock saves their spot (the sidebar shows Stage n/N); falling below fallY or standing on one of killBlocks sends them back to it (or to the start, with killSendsToStart), as does dying. -        code: '// Parkour: race from the start to the finish block. A checkpoint block saves your progress; falling, a kill block or\n// dying sends you back to it. /restart starts again. With CONFIG.buildCourse the game builds the course itself, in\n// stages that get harder.\nconst checkpoints = {}\nconst checkpointCounts = {}\nlet courseStarted = false\nlet coursePlan = []\n\nfunction onPlayerJoin(playerId) {\n\tif (CONFIG.buildCourse && !courseStarted) {\n\t\tcourseStarted = true\n\t\tcoursePlan = planCourse()\n\t\tconst start = CONFIG.startPosition\n\t\twhenWorldLoaded([start[0], start[1] - 1, start[2]], () => placeCourse(coursePlan))\n\t}\n\tsendToStart(playerId)\n\tapi.sendMessage(playerId, "Reach the " + CONFIG.finishBlock + "! Stand on " + CONFIG.checkpointBlock + " to save your progress. Type /restart to start again.", { color: "aqua" })\n}\n\nfunction stageCount() {\n\treturn Math.max(1, Math.min(50, Math.floor(CONFIG.stages)))\n}\n\n// The course as a list of parts { from, to, block, stage, pad }, going east from startPosition. A jump is never\n// longer than players can make: a gap of 3 blocks on the flat or down, 2 going up. Stages get harder: bigger gaps,\n// small rises and drops, narrower and shorter platforms. Change this to change the course\'s shape.\nfunction planCourse() {\n\tconst start = CONFIG.startPosition.map(Math.floor)\n\tif (CONFIG.courseShape === "tower") {\n\t\treturn planTower(start)\n\t}\n\tconst rises = [1, 0, 1, -1, 0, -1, 1, 1, -1, -1]\n\tconst stages = stageCount()\n\tconst jumps = Math.max(1, Math.min(20, Math.floor(CONFIG.jumpsPerStage)))\n\tconst parts = []\n\tlet y = start[1] - 1\n\tlet end = 0 // the east end of the last part, counted from the start\n\tfunction add(first, length, wide, block, stage, pad) {\n\t\tend = first + length - 1\n\t\tparts.push({ from: [start[0] + first, y, start[2] - wide], to: [start[0] + end, y, start[2] + wide], block: block, stage: stage, pad: pad })\n\t}\n\tlet count = 0\n\tfor (let stage = 1; stage <= stages; stage++) {\n\t\tconst hard = stages > 1 ? (stage - 1) / (stages - 1) : 0\n\t\tfor (let jump = 0; jump <= jumps; jump++) {\n\t\t\tconst pad = jump === 0\n\t\t\tif (stage === 1 && pad) {\n\t\t\t\tadd(-1, 3, 1, CONFIG.checkpointBlock, 1, true)\n\t\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t\tconst wanted = hard < 0.2 ? 0 : rises[count % rises.length]\n\t\t\tconst rise = y + wanted < start[1] - 3 ? 0 : wanted\n\t\t\tlet gap = count % 2 === 0 ? 1 + Math.round(hard * 2) : Math.max(1, Math.round(hard * 2))\n\t\t\tgap = Math.min(gap, rise > 0 ? 2 : 3)\n\t\t\tcount++\n\t\t\ty += rise\n\t\t\tif (pad) {\n\t\t\t\tadd(end + gap + 1, 3, 1, CONFIG.checkpointBlock, stage, true)\n\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\tadd(end + gap + 1, hard < 0.7 ? 2 : 1, hard < 0.5 ? 1 : 0, CONFIG.courseBlock, stage, false)\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tadd(end + 3, 3, 1, CONFIG.finishBlock, stages, false)\n\treturn parts\n}\n\n// The tower: platforms on a 9 by 9 square ring with the start at a corner, each one a block higher than the last, with\n// gaps of 1 to 2 blocks (the most a jump up can clear), smaller platforms as the stages go up\nfunction planTower(start) {\n\tconst side = 8\n\tconst stages = stageCount()\n\tconst jumps = Math.max(1, Math.min(20, Math.floor(CONFIG.jumpsPerStage)))\n\tconst parts = []\n\tlet along = 0 // how far round the ring\n\tlet y = start[1] - 1\n\tlet wide = 1\n\tlet last = [0, 0]\n\tfunction ringSpot(at) {\n\t\tconst offset = at % side\n\t\tconst edge = Math.floor(at / side) % 4\n\t\treturn edge === 0 ? [offset, 0] : edge === 1 ? [side, offset] : edge === 2 ? [side - offset, side] : [0, side - offset]\n\t}\n\tfunction add(width, block, stage, pad) {\n\t\tconst spot = ringSpot(along)\n\t\tparts.push({ from: [start[0] + spot[0] - width, y, start[2] + spot[1] - width], to: [start[0] + spot[0] + width, y, start[2] + spot[1] + width], block: block, stage: stage, pad: pad })\n\t\twide = width\n\t\tlast = spot\n\t}\n\t// Goes round the ring until the next platform is gap blocks from the last one, edge to edge (less far round at corners)\n\tfunction moveOn(gap, width) {\n\t\tlet spot\n\t\tdo {\n\t\t\talong++\n\t\t\tspot = ringSpot(along)\n\t\t} while (Math.max(Math.abs(spot[0] - last[0]), Math.abs(spot[1] - last[1])) - wide - width - 1 < gap)\n\t}\n\tadd(1, CONFIG.checkpointBlock, 1, true)\n\tfor (let stage = 1; stage <= stages; stage++) {\n\t\tconst hard = stages > 1 ? (stage - 1) / (stages - 1) : 0\n\t\tfor (let jump = stage === 1 ? 1 : 0; jump <= jumps; jump++) {\n\t\t\tconst pad = jump === 0\n\t\t\tconst width = pad || hard < 0.5 ? 1 : 0\n\t\t\tconst gap = hard < 0.3 ? 1 : 2\n\t\t\tmoveOn(gap, width)\n\t\t\ty += 1\n\t\t\tadd(width, pad ? -        code: '// Zombie waves: mobs come in waves around spawnCenter, each wave bigger than the last. Kill them for coins and get\n// ready in the break between waves. -        howItPlays: "Players wait at lobbyPosition. Winners of a minigame get pointsForWin points; falling out or dying puts a player out to watch above the arena until the next minigame. When roundSeconds run out the players still in win it. The sidebar shows the minigame, time left and the top 3. After gamesPerParty minigames the player with the most points wins the party (+1 saved partyWins), points start from 0 again and a new party starts.",

Then everyone comes back to the lobby for the next vote.\nconst restSeconds = 5 // seconds in the lobby after a game, before the next vote\nlet phase = "waiting" // "waiting", "voting", "playing" or "resting"\nlet currentGame = null // the game being played: [name, spawnPosition, gameSeconds]\nlet gameNumber = 0\nlet startedWith = 0 // players in the game when it started\n\nfunction onPlayerJoin(playerId) {\n\tif (phase === "playing") {\n\t\teliminate(playerId)\n\t\tgoTo(playerId, currentGame[1])\n\t\tapi.sendMessage(playerId, currentGame[0] + " is on! -        howItPlays: 'Joining shows welcomeMessage, the rules and the commands; /rules shows the rules again. /spawn sends a player to spawnPosition. With allowTpa, /tpa <name> asks that player, who types /tpaccept (or /tpdeny) within a minute. Players named in admins are admins: with adminCommands on they get /kick <name>, /tp <name> (go to them), /tphere <name> (bring them) and /announce <text>. When friendsOnly has names, anyone else who joins is kicked with a message (admins always get in). Nobody but admins can break or place blocks within spawnProtectRadius blocks of spawnPosition (side to side, any height). With killFeed, everyone is told "Alice killed Bob", "Bob was killed by a Draugr Zombie", or "Bob died" when they respawn after any other death (a fall, lava). With pvp "off" players can\'t hurt each other anywhere. With respawnProtectSeconds, a player who respawns can\'t be hurt by players for that long (hitting someone ends it early) and is told so; Bloxd itself already protects them for the first 5 seconds. With noHostileMobs, mobs that attack on sight (zombies, skeletons, golems, bears) that the world spawns by itself are taken away at once; mobs spawnMobs spawns stay, and so do api.attemptSpawnMob\'s unless put exactly in a block\'s middle (x and z ending in .5). With payCommand, /pay <name> <amount> gives that many of the player\'s coins to another player. Names can be typed in any case or just their start: /tp ali. Other code can call isAdmin(playerId).',

-        code: '// Server basics: a welcome message and the rules when a player joins, /rules, /spawn, /tpa to visit a friend, admin\n// commands (/kick, /tp, /tphere, /announce) for the names in admins, a friends-only list, and spawn protection.\nconst tpaRequests = {}\n// When each respawned player\'s protection from other players ends (an api.now() time)\nconst protectedUntil = {}\n// Players whose death the kill feed told already\nconst killTold = {}\nconst hostileMobsToRemove = []\n\nfunction sameName(a, b) {\n\treturn String(a).toLowerCase() === String(b).toLowerCase()\n}\n\nfunction isAdmin(playerId) {\n\treturn CONFIG.admins.some((name) => sameName(name, api.getEntityName(playerId)))\n}\n\n// A player in the world by name, in any case, or by the start of their name\nfunction findPlayer(name) {\n\tconst wanted = String(name || "").toLowerCase()\n\tconst ids = api.getPlayerIds()\n\tif (wanted === "") {\n\t\treturn null\n\t}\n\treturn ids.find((id) => sameName(api.getEntityName(id), wanted)) || ids.find((id) => api.getEntityName(id).toLowerCase().startsWith(wanted)) || null\n}\n\nfunction onPlayerJoin(playerId) {\n\tconst name = api.getEntityName(playerId)\n\tif (CONFIG.friendsOnly.length > 0 && !isAdmin(playerId) && !CONFIG.friendsOnly.some((friend) => sameName(friend, name))) {\n\t\tapi.kickPlayer(playerId, "Sorry, only the owner\'s friends can join this world.")\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tapi.sendMessage(playerId, CONFIG.welcomeMessage, { color: "lime" })\n\tshowRules(playerId)\n\tconst commands = ["/rules", "/spawn"].concat(CONFIG.allowTpa ? ["/tpa <name>"] : [], CONFIG.payCommand ? ["/pay <name> <amount>"] : [], CONFIG.adminCommands && isAdmin(playerId) ? ["/kick", "/tp", "/tphere", "/announce"] : [])\n\tapi.sendMessage(playerId, "Commands: " + commands.join(", "), { color: "yellow" })\n}\n\nfunction showRules(playerId) {\n\tif (CONFIG.rules.length > 0) {\n\t\tapi.sendMessage(playerId, "Rules:\\n" + CONFIG.rules.map((rule, index) => index + 1 + ". " + rule).join("\\n"), { color: "aqua" })\n\t}\n}\n\nfunction askToTeleport(playerId, name) {\n\tconst target = findPlayer(name)\n\tif (target === null || target === playerId) {\n\t\tapi.sendMessage(playerId, "Type /tpa and the name of a player in the world, like /tpa Alex.", { color: "orange" })\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\ttpaRequests[target] = { from: playerId, at: api.now() }\n\tapi.sendMessage(target, api.getEntityName(playerId) + " wants to teleport to you. "Teleported them to you." : "Said no.", { color: "lime" })\n}\n\n// The admin commands; true when the command was one of them\nfunction adminCommand(playerId, word, rest) {\n\tif (["kick", "tp", "tphere", "announce"].indexOf(word) === -1) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tif (!isAdmin(playerId)) {\n\t\tapi.sendMessage(playerId, "Only admins can use /" + word + ".", { color: "orange" })\n\t\treturn true\n\t}\n\tif (word === "announce" && rest !== "") {\n\t\tannounce(rest, "gold")\n\t\treturn true\n\t}\n\tconst target = word === "announce" ? null : findPlayer(rest)\n\tif (target === null || target === playerId) {\n\t\tapi.sendMessage(playerId, "Type /" + word + (word === "announce" ? " and your message." : " and the name of a player in the world."), { color: "orange" })\n\t} else if (word === "kick") {\n\t\tapi.kickPlayer(target, "You were kicked by an admin.")\n\t\tapi.broadcastMessage(api.getEntityName(target) + " was kicked.", { color: "orange" })\n\t} else if (word === "tp") {\n\t\tapi.setPosition(playerId, api.getPosition(target))\n\t} else {\n\t\tapi.setPosition(target, api.getPosition(playerId))\n\t\tapi.sendMessage(target, "An admin brought you to them.", { color: "yellow" })\n\t}\n\treturn true\n}\n\n// /pay <name> <amount>: moves whole coins from the player to another player\nfunction pay(playerId, rest) {\n\tconst words = rest.split(" ").filter((w) => w !== "")\n\tconst amount = Number(words.pop())\n\tconst target = findPlayer(words.join(" "))\n\tif (target !== null && target === playerId) {\n\t\tapi.sendMessage(playerId, "You can\'t pay yourself.", { color: "orange" })\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tif (target === null || !Number.isInteger(amount) || amount <= 0) {\n\t\tapi.sendMessage(playerId, "Type /pay, a player\'s name and how many coins, like /pay Alex 10.", { color: "orange" })\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\t// The coins another prefab or addCoins gives; read straight, so a world without coins doesn\'t get them from this\n\tconst have = api.getCurrencyAmount(playerId, "coins")\n\tconst theirs = api.getCurrencyAmount(target, "coins")\n\tif (have === null || theirs === null) {\n\t\tapi.sendMessage(playerId, "There are no coins in this world to pay with.", { color: "orange" })\n\t} else if (have < amount) {\n\t\tapi.sendMessage(playerId, "You only have " + have + " coins.", { color: "orange" })\n\t} else {\n\t\t// Not addCoins: a double-coins event doesn\'t double coins that are only moved\n\t\tapi.setCurrencyAmount(playerId, "coins", have - CONFIG.spawnPosition[0]) <= radius && Math.abs(z - CONFIG.spawnPosition[2]) <= radius && !isAdmin(playerId)) {\n\t\tapi.sendMessage(playerId, "Blocks near spawn are protected.", { color: "orange" })\n\t\treturn "preventChange"\n\t}\n}\n\n// PvP off stops all damage between players; a player who just respawned can\'t be hurt by players until they hit someone\nfunction onPlayerDamagingOtherPlayer(attackingPlayer, damagedPlayer) {\n\tif (CONFIG.pvp === "off" || api.now() < (protectedUntil[damagedPlayer] || 0)) {\n\t\treturn "preventDamage"\n\t}\n\tdelete protectedUntil[attackingPlayer]\n}\n\n// Every death ends with a respawn request: one nobody was told about (a fall, lava, the void) is told now\nfunction onRespawnRequest(playerId) {\n\tif (CONFIG.killFeed && !killTold[playerId]) {\n\t\tapi.broadcastMessage(api.getEntityName(playerId) + " died", { color: "red" })\n\t}\n\tdelete killTold[playerId]\n\tif (CONFIG.respawnProtectSeconds > 0) {\n\t\tprotectedUntil[playerId] = api.now() + CONFIG.respawnProtectSeconds * 1000\n\t\tapi.sendMessage(playerId, "Other players can\'t hurt you for " + CONFIG.respawnProtectSeconds + " seconds.", { color: "aqua" })\n\t}\n}\n\n// Kill feed: who killed who, told to everyone\nfunction onPlayerKilledOtherPlayer(attackingPlayer, killedPlayer) {\n\tif (CONFIG.killFeed) {\n\t\tconst killed = api.getEntityName(killedPlayer)\n\t\tapi.broadcastMessage(attackingPlayer === killedPlayer ? killed + " died" : api.getEntityName(attackingPlayer) + " killed " + killed, { color: "red" })\n\t\tkillTold[killedPlayer] = true\n\t}\n}\n\nfunction onMobKilledPlayer(attackingMob, killedPlayer) {\n\tif (CONFIG.killFeed) {\n\t\tapi.broadcastMessage(api.getEntityName(killedPlayer) + " was killed by a " + api.getEntityType(attackingMob), { color: "red" })\n\t\tkillTold[killedPlayer] = true\n\t}\n}\n\n// Mobs that attack on sight and that the world spawned by itself are taken away on the next tick. The world puts its\n// own in the middle of a block, x and z ending in .5 and y whole; code\'s spawns go through this too, so a mob that\n// spawnMobs keeps stays wherever it is\nfunction onWorldSpawnMob(mobId, mobType, x, y, z) {\n\tconst blockMiddle = Math.abs(x % 1) === 0.5 && Math.abs(z % 1) === 0.5 && y % 1 === 0\n\tif (CONFIG.noHostileMobs && blockMiddle && api.getDefaultMobSetting(mobType, "hostilityRadius") > 0) {\n\t\thostileMobsToRemove.push(mobId)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunction tick() {\n\twhile (hostileMobsToRemove.length > 0) {\n\t\tconst mobId = hostileMobsToRemove.pop()\n\t\tif (typeof spawnedMobs === "undefined" || spawnedMobs.indexOf(mobId) === -1) {\n\t\t\tapi.despawnMob(mobId)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunction onPlayerLeave(playerId) {\n\tdelete tpaRequests[playerId]\n\tdelete protectedUntil[playerId]\n\tdelete killTold[playerId]\n}',

-        code: "// Ready-made timers: runLater(seconds, fn) runs fn once after some seconds, repeatEvery(seconds, fn) runs it every\n// few seconds, and cancelTimer(id) stops either. Time is counted in tick. The list is a var made on first use, so\n// they can be called from the top of the file, above this code.\nvar timerList\nvar nextTimerId\n\nfunction runLater(seconds, fn) {\n\treturn addToTimerList(seconds, 0, fn)\n}\n\nfunction repeatEvery(seconds, fn) {\n\treturn addToTimerList(seconds, Math.max(50, seconds * 1000), fn)\n}\n\nfunction addToTimerList(seconds, everyMs, fn) {\n\tif (!timerList) {\n\t\ttimerList = []\n\t\tnextTimerId = 1\n\t}\n\tconst id = nextTimerId++\n\ttimerList.push({ id: id, msLeft: seconds * 1000, everyMs: everyMs, fn: fn })\n\treturn id\n}\n\nfunction cancelTimer(id) {\n\tconst index = timerList ? timerList.findIndex((timer) => timer.id === id) : -1\n\tif (index !== -1) {\n\t\ttimerList.splice(index, 1)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunction tick(ms) {\n\tif (!timerList) {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tfor (const timer of timerList.slice()) {\n\t\tif (!timerList.includes(timer)) {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\ttimer.msLeft -= ms\n\t\tif (timer.msLeft > 0) {\n\t\t\tcontinue\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (timer.everyMs > 0) {\n\t\t\ttimer.msLeft += timer.everyMs\n\t\t} else {\n\t\t\tcancelTimer(timer.id)\n\t\t}\n\t\ttimer.fn()\n\t}\n}",

-        code: '// Ready-made countdown: startCountdown(seconds, onDone) shows the seconds left big in the middle of everyone\'s screen,\n// then "Go!", then runs onDone. cancelCountdown() stops it.\nlet countdownTimer = null\nlet countdownClearTimer = null\n\nfunction startCountdown(seconds, onDone) {\n\tcancelCountdown()\n\tlet left = Math.max(1, Math.round(seconds))\n\tshowCountdownText(String(left))\n\tcountdownTimer = repeatEvery(1, () => {\n\t\tleft--\n\t\tif (left > 0) {\n\t\t\tshowCountdownText(String(left))\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\tcancelCountdown()\n\t\tshowCountdownText("Go!")\n\t\tcountdownClearTimer = runLater(1, () => {\n\t\t\tcountdownClearTimer = null\n\t\t\tshowCountdownText("")\n\t\t})\n\t\tonDone()\n\t})\n}\n\n// A countdown stopped part way takes its number off the screen too\nfunction cancelCountdown() {\n\tif (countdownTimer === null && countdownClearTimer === null) {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tcancelTimer(countdownTimer)\n\tcancelTimer(countdownClearTimer)\n\tcountdownTimer = null\n\tcountdownClearTimer = null\n\tshowCountdownText("")\n}\n\nfunction showCountdownText(text) {\n\tfor (const playerId of api.getPlayerIds()) {\n\t\tapi.setClientOption(playerId, "middleTextUpper", text)\n\t}\n}',

seconds (0: no limit)\n\tbreakSeconds: 5, // pause after a round before the next countdown\n}\n\n// Ready-made rounds: once CONFIG.minPlayers are in, a countdown runs and a round starts, calling your beginRound()\n// if you define one. endRound(message) ends it (so does the time running out), calling your finishRound(), and the\n// next countdown starts after a break. isRoundRunning() says whether a round is on.\nlet roundPhase = "waiting"\nlet roundMsLeft = 0\n\nfunction isRoundRunning() {\n\treturn roundPhase === "playing"\n}\n\nfunction roundSecondsLeft() {\n\treturn Math.max(0, Big boxes are filled in\n// parts of 7 x 7 x 7, as one api.setBlockRect fills at most 360 blocks, and a part whose blocks haven\'t loaded yet is\n// filled once they have.\nfunction fillBox(corner1, corner2, blockName) {\n\tconst low = [0, 1, 2].map((i) => Math.floor(Math.min(corner1[i], corner2[i])))\n\tconst high = [0, 1, 2].map((i) => Math.floor(Math.max(corner1[i], corner2[i])))\n\tconst step = 7\n\tfor (let x = low[0]; x <= high[0]; x += step) {\n\t\tfor (let y = low[1]; y <= high[1]; y += step) {\n\t\t\tfor (let z = low[2]; z <= high[2]; z += step) {\n\t\t\t\tconst from = [x, y, z]\n\t\t\t\tconst to = [Math.min(x + step - 1, high[0]), Math.min(y + step - 1, high[1]), Math.min(z + step - 1, high[2])]\n\t\t\t\tif (api.getBlock(from[0], from[1], from[2]) === "Unloaded" || api.getBlock(to[0], to[1], to[2]) === "Unloaded") {\n\t\t\t\t\twhenWorldLoaded(from, () => whenWorldLoaded(to, () => api.setBlockRect(from, to, blockName)))\n\t\t\t\t} else {\n\t\t\t\t\tapi.setBlockRect(from, to, blockName)\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t}\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}\n\nfunction buildPlatform(center, radius, blockName) {\n\tconst x = Math.floor(center[0])\n\tconst y = Math.floor(center[1])\n\tconst z = Math.floor(center[2])\n\tfillBox([x - radius, y, z - radius], [x + radius, y, z + radius], blockName)\n}',

The list is\n// a var made on first use, so it can be called from the top of the file.\nvar worldLoadWaits\n\nfunction whenWorldLoaded(position, fn) {\n\tif (!worldLoadWaits) {\n\t\tworldLoadWaits = []\n\t}\n\tworldLoadWaits.push({ position: position, fn: fn })\n}\n\nfunction tick(ms) {\n\tif (!worldLoadWaits) {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tfor (const wait of worldLoadWaits.slice()) {\n\t\tif (api.getBlock(wait.position[0], wait.position[1], wait.position[2]) !== "Unloaded") {\n\t\t\tworldLoadWaits.splice(worldLoadWaits.indexOf(wait), 1)\n\t\t\twait.fn()\n\t\t}\n\t}\n}',

The list is a var made on first use.\nvar shotList\nvar blastList\n\nfunction shootProjectile(playerId, options) {\n\tconst o = options || {}\n\tconst item = o.item || "Arrow"\n\tconst facing = api.getPlayerFacingInfo(playerId)\n\tconst gravity = o.gravity === undefined ? 1 : Math.max(0, o.gravity)\n\tconst shotId = api.attemptCreateThrowable(playerId, item, facing.camPos, facing.dir, o.speed || 1, 1, gravity)\n\tif (shotId !== null && (o.damage !== undefined || o.onHit)) {\n\t\tif (!shotList) {\n\t\t\tshotList = []\n\t\t}\n\t\tshotList.push({ id: shotId, playerId: playerId, item: item, damage: o.damage, onHit: o.onHit, until: Date.now() + 10000 })\n\t}\n\treturn shotId\n}\n\n// What the engine calls the blast of a shot that explodes: "Fireball Block", but "Rocket" for an RPG\'s\nfunction shotBlastName(item) {\n\tconst named = { "RPG": "Rocket", "Obby RPG": "Obby Rocket", "Super RPG": "Super Rocket", "Grenade Launcher": "Grenade", "Capitano Grenade": "Capitano Grenade" }\n\treturn named[item] || item + " Block"\n}\n\n// The engine says who hit whom with which item: the shooter\'s oldest flying shot of that item is the one that hit. The list is a var made on first use.\nvar eventsRunning\n\nfunction randomEvents(everySeconds, events) {\n\tif (!eventsRunning) {\n\t\teventsRunning = {}\n\t}\n\t// [name, start] and [name, start, end] work too\n\tconst list = events.map((entry) => {\n\t\treturn Array.isArray(entry) ? { name: entry[0], start: entry[1], end: entry[2] } : entry\n\t})\n\tlet lastEvent = null\n\tlet busy = false\n\treturn repeatEvery(everySeconds, () => {\n\t\tif (busy || list.length === 0 || api.getPlayerIds().length === 0) {\n\t\t\treturn\n\t\t}\n\t\t// Never the event just before: the same one, not the same name, so events without names still take turns\n\t\tconst choices = list.length > 1 ? list.filter((event) => event !== lastEvent) : list\n\t\tconst event = choices[Math.floor(Math.random() * choices.length)]\n\t\tconst name = event.name || "Event"\n\t\tconst key = String(name).toLowerCase()\n\t\tconst seconds = event.seconds !== undefined ? event.seconds : event.end ? 30 : 0\n\t\tlastEvent = event\n\t\tannounce("Event: " + name + "!", "gold")\n\t\tif (seconds > 0) {\n\t\t\tbusy = true\n\t\t\teventsRunning[key] = (eventsRunning[key] || 0) + 1\n\t\t\trunLater(seconds, () => {\n\t\t\t\tbusy = false\n\t\t\t\teventsRunning[key] = Math.max(0, eventsRunning[key] - 1)\n\t\t\t\tif (event.end) {\n\t\t\t\t\tevent.end()\n\t\t\t\t}\n\t\t\t\tannounce(name + " is over!", "gray")\n\t\t\t})\n\t\t}\n\t\tif (event.start) {\n\t\t\tevent.start()\n\t\t}\n\t\t// Over at once (seconds: 0): its end runs straight after\n\t\tif (seconds <= 0 && event.end) {\n\t\t\tevent.end()\n\t\t}\n\t})\n}\n\nfunction isEventOn(name) {\n\tif (!eventsRunning) {\n\t\treturn false\n\t}\n\tif (name === undefined) {\n\t\treturn Object.keys(eventsRunning).some((key) => eventsRunning[key] > 0)\n\t}\n\treturn (eventsRunning[String(name).toLowerCase()] || 0) > 0\n}',

It updates\n// by itself every second, beside other sidebar lines (setSidebar). hideLeaderboard(title) takes it away. The list is a\n// var made on first use, so showLeaderboard can be called from the top of the file.\nvar leaderboards\n\nfunction showLeaderboard(title, getValue, count) {\n\tif (!leaderboards) {\n\t\tleaderboards = {}\n\t}\n\thideLeaderboard(title)\n\tconst board = { title: String(title), getValue: getValue, rows: Math.max(1, Math.min(Math.floor(count || 5), 10)), shown: {}, timer: null }\n\tleaderboards[board.title] = board\n\tboard.timer = repeatEvery(1, () => {\n\t\tupdateLeaderboardRows(board)\n\t})\n\t// The first time is soon, not a second away, and not now: at the top of the file the world isn\'t ready\n\trunLater(0.1, () => {\n\t\tif (leaderboards[board.title] === board) {\n\t\t\tupdateLeaderboardRows(board)\n\t\t}\n\t})\n\treturn board.timer\n}\n\nfunction hideLeaderboard(title) {\n\tconst board = leaderboards ? leaderboards[String(title)] : null\n\tif (!board) {\n\t\treturn\n\t}\n\tcancelTimer(board.timer)\n\tdelete leaderboards[board.title]\n\tfor (const playerId of api.getPlayerIds()) {\n\t\tremoveSidebar(playerId, board.title)\n\t}\n}\n\nfunction updateLeaderboardRows(board) {\n\tconst playerIds = api.getPlayerIds()\n\tconst values = {}\n\tfor (const playerId of playerIds) {\n\t\tconst value = typeof board.getValue === "function" ? board.getValue(playerId) : board.getValue[playerId]\n\t\tvalues[playerId] = Math.round((Number(value) || 0) * 100) / 100\n\t}\n\tconst ranked = playerIds.slice().sort((a, b) => values[b] - values[a])\n\tconst lines = ranked.slice(0, board.rows).map((playerId, i) => (i + 1) + ". " + api.getEntityName(playerId) + " " + values[playerId])\n\tconst shown = {}\n\tfor (const playerId of playerIds) {\n\t\tlet text = "\\n" + lines.join("\\n")\n\t\tconst rank = ranked.indexOf(playerId)\n\t\tif (rank >= board.rows) {\n\t\t\ttext += "\\nYou: #" + (rank + 1) + " " + values[playerId]\n\t\t}\n\t\tshown[playerId] = text\n\t\t// Only a changed board is sent again\n\t\tif (board.shown[playerId] !== text) {\n\t\t\tsetSidebar(playerId, board.title, text)\n\t\t}\n\t}\n\tboard.shown = shown\n}\n\nfunction onPlayerJoin(playerId) {\n\t// A moment later, once the game\'s own onPlayerJoin has set the player up for the value to be read\n\trunLater(0.2, () => {\n\t\tfor (const title of Object.keys(leaderboards || {})) {\n\t\t\tupdateLeaderboardRows(leaderboards[title])\n\t\t}\n\t})\n}',

+      id: "readme",
+      title: "Getting started",
+      content: '# Getting started\n\nThere are three places to write JavaScript in Bloxd: code blocks, code boards and World Code. Code in any of them controls the game through `api`, in custom games and worlds. Only players who can edit code (the `canEditCode` client option) can write it, but anyone can run a code block or board.\n\nPlease use [our Discord](https://discord.gg/playbloxd) to report problems or suggest features.\n\n## Code Blocks\n\n- Find the Code Block by searching in the creative menu.\n- Clicking a code block runs its code, unless you are crouching. Players who can edit code open its code by right clicking it.\n- Running a code block or board also runs the code blocks and boards touching it, so clicking a `press to code` board next to a code block runs it without opening the code editor.\n- A code block doesn\'t need a `press to code` line, and removes one if you add it.\n\n## Boards\n\n- A board whose text starts with `press to code` on its own line runs the code below that line when someone clicks it.\n- Boards only hold a little text: use a code block for anything longer, or split the code across several boards.\n\n## World Code\n\nWorld Code runs for the whole world instead of when someone clicks. Open it with F8. It defines [Callbacks](#callbacks), such as `tick` and `onPlayerJoin`, which the game calls when things happen. The [How-Tos](#howTo) build whole games with it.\n\n## Globals\n\n| Name | Value |\n|------|-------|\n| `api` | The game API: every method in the [API Reference](#apiReference) |\n| `myId` | The ID of the player running the code, or `null` when nobody is, as in most World Code |\n| `playerId` | The same as `myId` |\n| `thisPos` | The position of the code block or board running the code, as `[x, y, z]` |\n| `api.ownerDbId` | The database ID of the world\'s owner, or `null` if it has none |\n\n## Logs and results\n\n- `api.log` and `console.log` do the same thing: each shows its values in chat as a `Log:` message.\n- When the last line of a code block or board has a value, the player who ran it sees that value as a `Result:` message.\n\n## Next steps\n\n[Snippets](#snippets) has short pieces of code to copy into a code block and change.\n\n## Glossary of Referenced Types\n\nThese \'types\' can\'t be referenced by your code, but they help explain some of the parameters in the API.\n\n```ts\ntype CustomTextStyling = (string | EntityName | TranslatedText | StyledIcon | StyledText | ProgressBar | StyledKeyBinding)[]\n\ntype EntityMeshScalingMap = {\n    [key in "TorsoNode" | "HeadMesh" | "ArmRightMesh" | "ArmLeftMesh" | "LegLeftMesh" | "LegRightMesh"]?: number[]\n}\n\ntype EntityName = {\n    entityName: string\n    style?: {\n        color?: string\n        colour?: string\n    }\n}\n\ntype IngameIconName = "Damage" | "Damage Reduction" | "Speed" | "VoidJump" | "Fist" | "Frozen" | "Hydrated" | "Invisible" | "Jump Boost" | "Poisoned" | "Slowness" | "Weakness" | +      content: '# Changelog\n\nHere you can discover the latest changes to the API.\n\n### 17th November 2026\n- Added the [`highlightedHotbarSlots`](#clientOptions-highlightedHotbarSlots) client option, to make hotbar slots pulse and show a player which item to use, e.g. `api.setClientOption(playerId, "highlightedHotbarSlots", [0])`. Set it to `[]` to stop.\n- A player who joins while an ad plays now enters the world only once the ad ends, so nothing can hurt them while they can\'t play. Turn this off in a round-based game with [`api.setJoinsWaitForAds(false)`](#apiReference-setJoinsWaitForAds), so a party\'s players are all in the lobby when a round starts. Games using the `@plugins/sessionBasedGame` plugin do this already.\n\n### 15th November 2026\n- Physics bodies now stop growing at 25 blocks wide and 90 tall, so a huge one can no longer freeze a world. [`api.setLifeformScale`](#apiReference-setLifeformScale) still grows the model by any scale, but past that size only the model grows: a player\'s body stops at scale 50. The same limit applies to a vehicle\'s `width` and `height` in [`api.setVehicleSetting`](#apiReference-setVehicleSetting), a collision box offset in [`api.setPlayerPhysicsState`](#apiReference-setPlayerPhysicsState), `physicsOpts` in [`api.attemptSpawnMob`](#apiReference-attemptSpawnMob), and the body of a mesh entity or item drop with physics. A mesh entity\'s collision box follows its body, so use `widthExpandAmt` and `heightExpandAmt` to make it bigger. Your code\'s log shows a warning the first time a value is capped.\n\n### 7th November 2026\n- A gun\'s `fireRate` is now the rate it fires at, and a `fireRate` gun stat override fires the gun at that rate. `api.getItemStat(null, gunName, "fireRate")` now gives TAR-21 128, Double Barrel 150, Striker-12 185, VSR 450 and FMR 450.\n- New `cadenceMs` gun stat: how fast spread recovers and shot sounds and the equip delay are paced, in ms; most guns use their fire interval, e.g. `{ fireRate: 300, cadenceMs: 150 }`.\n\n### 5th November 2026\n- Added the [`gameCamera`](#clientOptions-gameCamera) client option, to take over a player\'s camera for top-down games, map flyovers, security cameras, spectating and cutscenes. Set its `mode`:\n  - `"fixed"` stands still at a `position`, e.g. `{ mode: "fixed", position: [0, 30, 0], lookAt: playerId }`.\n  - `"follow"` moves with the player or another entity at an `offset`, e.g. a top-down view with `{ mode: "follow", offset: [0, 20, 5] }`, or `{ mode: "follow", target: otherPlayerId, offset: [0, 3, -6], offsetSpace: "target", avoidTerrain: true }` to spectate from behind.\n  - `"path"` flies through `keyframes` of `{ timeMs, position, lookAt }`.\n  - `"frame"` keeps several players or positions in view, e.g. `{ mode: "frame", targets: api.getPlayerIds().slice(0, 64) }`.\n  - `"default"` goes back to the player\'s own camera.\n- Every camera takes `blendInMs` to glide there from the current view, and the others take `fov` in degrees, `playerLook` to let the mouse look around, and `playerFacing` to choose which way the player turns while walking. To replay the same path, set another camera first.\n- For cutscenes, every camera also takes `transition` to fade through a colour instead of blending, `letterbox: true` for black bars at the top and bottom of the screen, and `hideHud: true` to hide the HUD, e.g. `{ mode: "path", keyframes, transition: { outMs: 500, holdMs: 250, inMs: 600 }, letterbox: true, hideHud: true }`, then `{ mode: "default", transition: { outMs: 500, holdMs: 250, inMs: 600 } }` to fade back to the player\'s own camera.\n- [`customButtons`](#clientOptions-customButtons) can now use `"Space"` as a button\'s `keycode`, shown as `_` next to the button, e.g. `{ id: "dash", icon: "bolt", keycode: "Space" }`. Space also jumps for players who have not changed their jump key.\n\n### 2nd November 2026\n- Colours in `CustomTextStyling` and text styles (`color` / `colour`, and a `ProgressBar`\'s `colours` and `backgroundColour`) must now be plain CSS colours: a name, hex or `rgb()`/`hsl()`-style colour, e.g. `"red"`, `"#ff0000"` or `"rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.5)"`, optionally followed by stop positions in a `ProgressBar`\'s `colours`, e.g. `"red 30%"`. Values with other CSS functions, such as `url()`, are refused with an error.\n\n### 26th October 2026\n- Added the [`lockHeadToBody`](#entitySettings-lockHeadToBody) entity setting. Set it on a mob, player or Person mesh entity to make it turn as one piece, so [`api.setEntityRotation`](#apiReference-setEntityRotation) sets where its whole body faces rather than turning its head first, e.g. `api.setTargetedPlayerSettingForEveryone(eId, "lockHeadToBody", true)`.\n- [`api.setMobAiState`](#apiReference-setMobAiState) takes an optional `{ hold: true }` to keep a mob in the state you set until you set another one: it won\'t time out, react to nearby players or fight back when hit. It still leaves the state if its target leaves the game or turns invisible, or if it is tamed. For example, `api.setMobAiState(mobId, "watching", { targetId: playerId }, { hold: true })` keeps a mob watching a player.\n\n### 23rd October 2026\n- Added the `@plugins/dialogue` plugin, whose `sayDialogue` shows a player a line for a while, 6 seconds by default, and `clearDialogue` hides it early. See the [dialogue how-to](#howTo-Dialogue) for examples.\n- The new [Dialogue Voices](#dialogueVoices) page lists every voice preset and explains how to build a custom `SpeechSynth`. Its dialogue editor lets you start from a preset, tune the voice, type a line to hear it read out, and copy the code.\n- Each docs page can now be copied as Markdown, or opened in ChatGPT or Claude to ask about it, from the buttons in its header. AI tools can also read every page as Markdown at `/docs/<page>.md`, with an index of them all at [bloxd.io/llms.txt](https://bloxd.io/llms.txt).\n\n### 22nd October 2026\n- The docs have a new home at [bloxd.io/docs](https://bloxd.io/docs), with a page for every reference, setting list, How-To and asset list, in light and dark themes and laid out for phones too.\n- New pages: [Getting started](#readme) explains code blocks, boards and World Code, [Snippets](#snippets) collects short examples to copy, and [Types](https://bloxd.io/docs/types), on the site, explains every type the reference mentions.\n- Press Ctrl K, or \u2318 K on a Mac, to search every method, callback, setting, guide and asset name, landing right on it.\n- Methods, callbacks and settings are cards you can filter and copy from. Hover a type in a signature to see what it is, and each card links to the guides that use it and the changelog entries that mention it. Deprecated methods are marked.\n- Asset pages show what each name looks like or sounds like: particle effects play live, sounds and songs play in a player with a scrubber and volume, NPC skins and poses are shown as the game draws them, and blocks and items show their textures.\n- The [Icons](#icons) page has a `CustomTextStyling` editor: add parts from a list, edit their styles and icons, and copy the code.\n- Every QTE can be played on the [QTEs](#qte) page, with its sensible defaults.\n- Added the [`dialogue`](#clientOptions-dialogue) client option! Set it to show a player a line of dialogue below the crosshair, revealed word by word in a voice, with the speaker\'s name above it, e.g. `api.setClientOption(playerId, "dialogue", { line: "Welcome!", speakerName: "Guide", voice: "regular" })`. Set it to `null` to hide the line.\n  - `voice` takes a preset, `"soft"`, `"regular"`, `"dark"`, `"high-pitched"`, `"gruff"`, `"lively"`, `"posh"` or `"mechanical"`, or a `SpeechSynth` that sets every parameter. Leave it out for a silent line.\n  - `[[Item Name]]` in a line shows that item\'s icon inline.\n\n### 16th October 2026\n- The damage callbacks ([`onPlayerDamagingOtherPlayer`](#callbacks-onPlayerDamagingOtherPlayer), [`onPlayerDamagingMob`](#callbacks-onPlayerDamagingMob), [`onMobDamagingPlayer`](#callbacks-onMobDamagingPlayer), [`onMobDamagingOtherMob`](#callbacks-onMobDamagingOtherMob)) now receive a last `damageInfo` argument whose `cause` says what dealt the hit: `"Melee"`, `"Projectile"`, `"Gun"`, `"Explosion"`, `"Spikes"`, `"Fall"`, `"Stomp"`, `"Thorns"` or `"Effect"`, or `null` when unknown. Use it to tell a swing of a held item from that item going off, e.g. a punch with a Mining Grenade in hand from a Mining Grenade\'s blast.\n- [`api.attemptApplyDamage`](#apiReference-attemptApplyDamage) takes an optional `damageCause`, passed on to those callbacks.\n\n### 30th September 2026\n- `interactable` now gives mobs the same interaction priority as mesh entities: `onPlayerAltAction` runs before held-item actions. Native harvesting, mounting and pet actions are disabled while the setting is true; leave it false for ordinary mob behaviour.\n\n### 29th September 2026\n- Added project schematics to World Code! Use the `+` beside "Schematics" in the Code Editor to upload a `.bloxdschem` file or choose a snapshot from your profile. Projects support up to five schematics.\n- Added [`api.setChunkAsSchematic`](#apiReference-setChunkAsSchematic) to replace one complete chunk, including air and block data. Positions are block coordinates selecting their containing chunks, like `copyChunk`.\n- Added [`api.getSchematicDimensions()`](#apiReference-getSchematicDimensions) to read a schematic\'s stored `[x, y, z]` dimensions, including selection padding.\n- `@plugins/sessionBasedGame` maps and lobbies now accept `source: { schematic: "maps/arena.bloxdschem" }` as an alternative to a world rectangle. Maps are pasted directly and must fit the available placement and block-data budgets.\n- Schematic saved from profiles are **snapshots** - you must update the schematic in the world/custom game if you edit the linked schematic otherwise.\n- See the [project schematics how-to](#howTo-Project schematics) for examples and details.\n\n### 10th September 2026\n- Added the `interactable` entity setting. Set it on a mesh entity or a mob (e.g. `api.setTargetedPlayerSettingForEveryone(eId, "interactable", true)`) to make alt actioning it count as an interaction: the alt action is consumed, so a held block isn\'t placed through the entity and a held throwable isn\'t used, and `onPlayerAltAction` fires with the entity as the target. Leave it off for decorative entities, or they will swallow player input. It also makes the entity pickable, so an entity can be `interactable` with `canAttack` off: the player\'s aim lands on it and interacting works, but swinging or shooting at it does nothing. On a mob it applies alongside the usual mounting and taming behaviour rather than replacing it, though there a held throwable or consumable is still used in preference to interacting.\n- Entities marked `interactable` now show an interaction prompt by the crosshair while a player is looking at them, showing the key bound to the interact action (`E` by default) so players can tell which input to use. Set the new `interactionPrompt` entity setting to replace the label beside that key, e.g. `api.setTargetedPlayerSettingForEveryone(eId, "interactionPrompt", "Open Shop")`, and leave it off for the default "Interact". It takes plain text or `CustomTextStyling`, and describes what interacting does rather than which button to press, since the engine draws the key itself. Not shown on touchscreens, where a tap needs no prompt.\n\n### 8th September 2026\n- Added first-party plugins!\n  - You can import helper scripts to help you from `@plugins`\n    - E.g. `import { setTimeout } from "@plugins/helpers"`\n  - See the [plugins how-to](#howTo-Plugins) for more information.\n\n  - The biggest example of this is **Session-Based Game**, a helper to help you create a game with mini-matches, like Bedwars/Skywars etc.\n    - `import { createGame } from "@plugins/sessionBasedGame"` to check it out\n    - See the [SessionBasedGame how-to](#howTo-Building a SessionBasedGame) for more information.\n\n### 28th August 2026\n- Added vehicle spawn callbacks:\n    - [`onPlayerAttemptSpawnVehicle`](#callbacks-onPlayerAttemptSpawnVehicle)\n    - [`onWorldAttemptSpawnVehicle`](#callbacks-onWorldAttemptSpawnVehicle)\n    - [`onPlayerSpawnVehicle`](#callbacks-onPlayerSpawnVehicle)\n    - [`onWorldSpawnVehicle`](#callbacks-onWorldSpawnVehicle)\n    - [`onVehicleDespawned`](#callbacks-onVehicleDespawned)\n- Added [`onEntityDeleted`](#callbacks-onEntityDeleted), called whenever any non-player entity is deleted.\n\n### 27th August 2026\n- Added [`api.attemptSpawnVehicle`](#apiReference-attemptSpawnVehicle) to spawn rideable vehicles (boats, karts, cars) which players can mount with an alt action.\n\n### 18th August 2026\n- Added TypeScript support to World Code!\n  - Rename your file from `index.js` to `index.ts` to use TypeScript files!\n  - Import some of our types from `@bloxd`\n    - E.g. `import type { PlayerId } from "@bloxd"`\n  - Use your own types!\n  - Type Checking is supported and errors will show if you use incorrect types.\n\n- Multiple files are supported! Split your code across multiple files for better readability!\n  - Create `.js` and `.ts` files\n  - Use `import` / `export` syntax to be able to import files across between versions\n  - `index.js` or `index.ts` MUST be where your callbacks are stored and cannot be imported anywhere else.\n  - `require()` syntax technically works although isn\'t type-safe.\n\n- Increased total code size from 64k characters to 512k characters.\n\n- Added variations to custom games!\n    - Each custom game can now have multiple variations, with `default` being the default variation.\n    - [`api.getVariation`](#apiReference-getVariation)\n    - [`api.matchmakeToVariation`](#apiReference-matchmakeToVariation)\n    - See the [variations doc](#howTo-Variations) for more information.\n\n### 11th August 2026\n- Added currency API:\n    - [`api.setCurrency`](#apiReference-setCurrency)\n    - [`api.getCurrency`](#apiReference-getCurrency)\n    - [`api.deleteCurrency`](#apiReference-deleteCurrency)\n    - [`api.getCurrencyAmount`](#apiReference-getCurrencyAmount)\n    - [`api.setCurrencyAmount`](#apiReference-setCurrencyAmount)\n    - [`api.giveCurrencyAmount`](#apiReference-giveCurrencyAmount)\n    - These currencies can be used in the `currency` field in the Shop to automatically deduct currency on purchase.\n    - These can also be persisted across sessions.\n\n### 10th August 2026\n- Added to the UI Request System:\n    - [`api.addUiRequestPopup`](#apiReference-addUiRequestPopup)\n\n### 7th August 2026\n- Added UI Request System:\n    - [`api.addUiRequest`](#apiReference-addUiRequest)\n    - [`api.deleteUiRequest`](#apiReference-deleteUiRequest)\n    - [`onUiRequestResponded`](#callbacks-onUiRequestResponded)\n\n### 20th July 2026\n- New mob settings:\n    - [`runningJumpInfo`](#mobSettings-runningJumpInfo)\n    - [`runningRandomFacingInfo`](#mobSettings-runningRandomFacingInfo)\n    - [`runningSlideInfo`](#mobSettings-runningSlideInfo)\n    - [`walkingJumpInfo`](#mobSettings-walkingJumpInfo)\n    - [`walkingRandomFacingInfo`](#mobSettings-walkingRandomFacingInfo)\n    - [`walkingSlideInfo`](#mobSettings-walkingSlideInfo)\n\n### 13th July 2026\n- Added new [`bridgeInfo`](#mobSettings-bridgeInfo) mob setting to make mobs build bridges or leave trails, e.g.:\n```js\nbridgeInfo: {\n    blockToPlace: "Bricks",\n    mustBeGrounded: false,\n    yOffset: -1,\n},\n```\n\n### 26th June 2026\n- Added new client options for custom game UI:\n    - [`middleTextTop`](#clientOptions-middleTextTop)\n    - [`headerChips`](#clientOptions-headerChips)\n- Added ProgressBar support to options that accept a CustomTextStyling\n    - e.g. `["Loading", { type: "ProgressBar", progress: 0.5 }]`\n\n### 15th June 2026\n- Added new client options for adjusting the third person camera:\n    - [`cameraRotationOffset`](#clientOptions-cameraRotationOffset)\n    - [`cameraPositionOffset`](#clientOptions-cameraPositionOffset)\n\n### 11th June 2026\n- Added the ability to get and set scale for lifeforms (players, mobs)\n    - [`api.getLifeformScale`](#apiReference-getLifeformScale)\n    - [`api.setLifeformScale`](#apiReference-setLifeformScale)\n\n- Added new block standing callbacks:\n    - This is to prevent having to use `onBlockStand`, which eats into your runtime limit significantly due to its high frequency of being called\n    - [`onBlockStandStart`](#callbacks-onBlockStandStart)\n    - [`onBlockStandStop`](#callbacks-onBlockStandStop)\n\n- Added `isReceiveDamageCooldownGlobal` [client option](#clientOptions-isReceiveDamageCooldownGlobal) and [mob setting](#mobSettings-isReceiveDamageCooldownGlobal)\n\n### 10th June 2026\n- Added [`showChatBubbles`](#clientOptions-showChatBubbles) client option\n- Added [`useRespawnButton`](#clientOptions-useRespawnButton) client option\n- Added [`multilineTextBox`](#entitySettings-multilineTextBox) entity setting\n- Added [`lobbyLeaderboardTags`](#entitySettings-lobbyLeaderboardTags) entity setting\n\n### 18th May 2026\n- Added the ability to change the gamemode of a player\n    - [`api.setPlayerGamemode`](#apiReference-setPlayerGamemode)\n    - [`api.getPlayerGamemode`](#apiReference-getPlayerGamemode)\n- Added the ability to queue text to be displayed in different places on the screen\n    - [`api.queueMiddleTextLower`](#apiReference-queueMiddleTextLower)\n    - [`api.queueMiddleTextUpper`](#apiReference-queueMiddleTextUpper)\n    - [`api.queueCrosshairText`](#apiReference-queueCrosshairText)\n    - [`api.getQueuedStatus`](#apiReference-getQueuedStatus)\n    - [`api.removeFromQueue`](#apiReference-removeFromQueue)\n\n### 15th May 2026\n- Significantly increased runtime limit - interrupts should be less frequent\n- Added [`api.isNearInterrupt`](#apiReference-isNearInterrupt)\n\n### 12th May 2026\n- Added new client option [`groundArrowPath`](#clientOptions-groundArrowPath)\n\n### 11th May 2026\n- Added Changelog\n- Added a bunch of new API Methods:\n    - [`api.addCustomKillfeedMessage`](#apiReference-addCustomKillfeedMessage)\n    - [`api.deleteAllItems`](#apiReference-deleteAllItems)\n    - [`api.findItem`](#apiReference-findItem)\n    - [`api.findStandardChestItem`](#apiReference-findStandardChestItem)\n    - [`api.getEffectLevel`](#apiReference-getEffectLevel)\n    - [`api.getItemDropName`](#apiReference-getItemDropName)\n    - [`api.getItemIDsOverlappingWithPlayer`](#apiReference-getItemIDsOverlappingWithPlayer)\n    - [`api.getMobDbId`](#apiReference-getMobDbId)\n    - [`api.hasEffect`](#apiReference-hasEffect)\n    - [`api.preventFallDamageNextGrounding`](#apiReference-preventFallDamageNextGrounding)\n    - [`api.removeItemNameFromStandardChest`](#apiReference-removeItemNameFromStandardChest)\n    - [`api.resetCanChangeBlock`](#apiReference-resetCanChangeBlock)\n    - [`api.resetCanPickUpItem`](#apiReference-resetCanPickUpItem)\n    - [`api.setOtherEntitySettingToDefault`](#apiReference-setOtherEntitySettingToDefault)\n    - [`api.updateMeshParticleSystems`](#apiReference-updateMeshParticleSystems)\n\n### 7th May 2026\n- Added [`api.copyChunk`](#apiReference-copyChunk)\n- Added [`onPlayerToggledShopMenu`](#callbacks-onPlayerToggledShopMenu)\n\n### 28th April 2026\n- Doubled code block size (16000 -> 32000)\n- \'Hide World Code\' option renamed to \'Hide Code\' and also hides code of Code Blocks\n- New [docs page!](https://bloxd.io/docs)\n\n### 23rd April 2026\n- Added [`api.matchmakePlayer`](#apiReference-matchmakePlayer)\n- Added per-item gun stats in `customAttributes.gunStats`\n\n### 21st April 2026\n- Added database methods to write persisted data to be saved between sessions.\n- There are two sections of database values:\n    - Lobby\n        - [`api.getLobbyDBValue`](#apiReference-getLobbyDBValue)\n        - [`api.setLobbyDBValue`](#apiReference-setLobbyDBValue)\n        - [`api.deleteLobbyDBValue`](#apiReference-deleteLobbyDBValue)\n        - [`api.deleteAllLobbyDBValues`](#apiReference-deleteAllLobbyDBValues)\n        - Writes data that is persisted to the *lobby*, whether it\'s a worlds lobby or a lobby within a custom game\n    - Player\n        - [`api.getDBValue`](#apiReference-getDBValue)\n        - [`api.setDBValue`](#apiReference-setDBValue)\n        - [`api.deletePlayerDBValue`](#apiReference-deletePlayerDBValue)\n        - [`api.deleteAllPlayerDBValues`](#apiReference-deleteAllPlayerDBValues)\n        - Writes data that is persisted to the player. For custom games, this data persists *between* lobbies\n\n### 16th April 2026\n- Added [`api.setItemStat`](#apiReference-setItemStat)\n\n### 11th April 2026\n- The Code Editor now supports **collaborative editing**\n    - You can now simultaneously code with your other fellow coders at the same time! Hop into a code block or World Code together to simultaneously create the best World or the best Custom Game ever!!\n\n### 7th April 2026\n- New Code Editor UI! Syntax Highlighting, Autocomplete, Error Checking, and more!\n\n### 25th March 2026\n- Increased world code size from 16000 to 64000 characters\n\n### 24th March 2026\n- Added mesh entities!\n    - [`api.attemptCreateMeshEntity`](#apiReference-attemptCreateMeshEntity)\n    - [`api.updateMeshEntity`](#apiReference-updateMeshEntity)\n    - [`api.deleteMeshEntity`](#apiReference-deleteMeshEntity)\n- Added throwables!\n    - [`api.attemptCreateThrowable`](#apiReference-attemptCreateThrowable)\n    - [`api.deleteThrowable`](#apiReference-deleteThrowable)\n\n### 23rd March 2026\n- Added the ability to open and close chests for players, going beyond reach distance to open chests from far away\n    - [`api.openChestForPlayer`](#apiReference-openChestForPlayer)\n    - [`api.closeChestForPlayer`](#apiReference-closeChestForPlayer)\n\n### Previous Changes\n- For previous changes, see the [code-api](https://github.com/Bloxdy/code-api) repository or #dev-log in the Bloxd Discord server'

+      id: "meshEntities",
+      title: "Mesh Entities",
+      content: '# Mesh Entities, Throwables & Node Mesh Attachment\n\nMesh entities are server-created 3D objects whose position is synced with all clients. Throwables are a specialised subset that use the engine\'s built-in projectile physics. Node mesh attachment lets you attach additional meshes to specific bones/nodes of an existing entity (e.g. a weapon on a player\'s hand).\n\n## Limits\n\n- `attemptCreateMeshEntity` returns `null` instead of throwing once the lobby reaches the limit for the entity it would create: 400 without physics (audio entities count too), 100 with physics (throwables count too).\n- Separately, each player sees only the nearest 100 mesh entities of one kind (the mesh type, or the block name for a `BloxdBlock`); farther ones are hidden.\n\n---\n\n## Mesh Entities\n\n### Mesh Types\n\nThe following mesh types are available, each with different options:\n\n- **`Box`**\n- **`BloxdBlock`**\n- **`Person`**\n- **`Leaderboard`**\n- **`ParticleEmitter`**\n\n#### `Box`\n\n```ts\ntype BoxOpts = {\n    hideDist?: number\n    meshOffset?: number[]\n    autoRotate?: boolean\n    lineToEId?: EntityId // EntityId to connect to using a line\n    width: number\n    height: number\n    depth: number\n    diffuseColor?: number[]\n    emissiveColor?: number[]\n    backFaceCulling?: boolean // Default true\n    texture?: string // Can be a blockname. Wraps every one block\n    faceUV?: number[][]\n    animateTexture?: boolean // If true, `texture` must be an animated block name (e.g. "Lava", "Red Portal") and the Box cycles through its frames.\n}\n```\n\n#### `BloxdBlock`\n\n```ts\ntype BloxdBlockOpts = {\n    hideDist?: number\n    meshOffset?: number[]\n    autoRotate?: boolean\n    lineToEId?: EntityId // EntityId to connect to using a line\n    blockName: BlockNameOrId\n    size: number | [number, number, number]\n    enchantmentTier?: EnchantmentTier // Enchantment sheen, drawn only when attached to an entity node, as a worn glider is.\n}\n```\n\n#### `Person`\n\n```ts\ntype PersonOpts = {\n    hideDist?: number\n    meshOffset?: number[]\n    autoRotate?: boolean\n    lineToEId?: EntityId // EntityId to connect to using a line\n    size?: number\n    textures?: Partial<Cosmetics>\n    pose?: PlayerPose\n}\n```\n\n#### `Leaderboard`\n\n```ts\ntype LeaderboardOpts = {\n    hideDist?: number\n    meshOffset?: number[]\n    autoRotate?: boolean\n    lineToEId?: EntityId // EntityId to connect to using a line\n    leaderboard: string\n    title?: string\n    scoreLabel?: string\n    size?: number // Uniform scale of the 2.5 by 3.75 block board. Defaults to 1.\n    width?: number // Absolute width in blocks, overriding the width derived from size.\n    height?: number // Absolute height in blocks, overriding the height derived from size.\n}\n```\n\n#### `ParticleEmitter`\n\n```ts\ntype ParticleEmitterOpts = {\n    texture: string\n    minLifeTime: number\n    maxLifeTime: number\n    minEmitPower: number\n    maxEmitPower: number\n    minSize: number\n    maxSize: number\n    gravity: number[]\n    velocityGradients: VelocityGradient[]\n    colorGradients: TimeColorGradient[] | RandomColorGradient[]\n    blendMode: ParticleSystemBlendMode\n    hideDist?: number\n    meshOffset?: number[]\n    autoRotate?: boolean\n    lineToEId?: EntityId // EntityId to connect to using a line\n    height: number\n    width: number\n    depth: number\n    emitRate: number\n    followTargetMeshOffset?: boolean // Include the followed lifeform\'s visual offset, including its vehicle seat.\n    emitterShape?: "box" | "ring" // Ring emits radially from the perimeter; width/depth set its diameters, height its thickness.\n    dir1?: number[]\n    dir2?: number[]\n}\n```\n\n### Creating a Mesh Entity\n\n```ts\n/**\n * Try to create a mesh entity. This creates an entity whose mesh position is synced with clients.\n * Set entity position using setPosition\n * There is a limit to the number of mesh entities that can be created: 400 without physics (audio entities count too), 100 with physics (throwables count too).\n * Separately, each player sees only the nearest 100 mesh entities of one kind (the mesh type, or the block name for a BloxdBlock); farther ones are hidden.\n *\n * @param {MeshType} type\n * @param {MeshEntityOpts[MeshType]} opts\n * @param {string} [name] - The default name for the nametag\n * @param {MeshEntityPhysicsOpts} [physicsOptions] - Physics Options. With doPhysics, the physics body is at most 25 blocks across, however big the mesh; the entity collision box is the body grown by widthExpandAmt and heightExpandAmt.\n * @param {EntityId} [initiatorId] - The entity that initiated the creation of the mesh entity.\n * @returns {EntityId | null} - null if the entity creation failed, otherwise the entity ID.\n */\nattemptCreateMeshEntity(type, opts, name, physicsOptions, initiatorId)\n```\n\nUse `api.setPosition()` to move the entity after creation.\n\n#### Examples\n\nCreate a red box:\n\n```ts\nconst boxId = api.attemptCreateMeshEntity("Box", {\n    width: 1,\n    height: 1,\n    depth: 1,\n    diffuseColor: [255, 0, 0],\n})\nif (boxId) {\n    api.setPosition(boxId, 10, 50, 10)\n}\n```\n\nCreate a Bloxd block mesh:\n\n```ts\nconst blockId = api.attemptCreateMeshEntity("BloxdBlock", {\n    blockName: "Block of Diamond",\n    size: 1,\n})\n```\n\nCreate a person mesh:\n\n```ts\nconst personId = api.attemptCreateMeshEntity("Person", {\n    size: 1,\n    pose: "standing",\n    textures: { head: "trader_black" },\n}, "Bedwars Merchant")\n```\n\nCreate a mesh entity with physics:\n\n```ts\nconst physicsBoxId = api.attemptCreateMeshEntity(\n    "Box",\n    { width: 0.5, height: 0.5, depth: 0.5, diffuseColor: [0, 255, 0] },\n    "",\n    {\n        doPhysics: true,\n        collidesEntities: true,\n        collideBits: 1,\n        collideMask: 1,\n    },\n)\n```\n\n### Updating a Mesh Entity\n\n```ts\n/**\n * Update a mesh entity. If used on a non-mesh entity, will do nothing.\n *\n * @param {EntityId} eId\n * @param {MeshType} type\n * @param {MeshEntityOpts[MeshType]} opts\n * @returns {void}\n */\nupdateMeshEntity(eId, type, opts)\n```\n\n```ts\napi.updateMeshEntity(boxId, "Box", {\n    width: 2,\n    height: 2,\n    depth: 2,\n    diffuseColor: [0, 0, 255],\n})\n```\n\n### Deleting a Mesh Entity\n\n```ts\n/**\n * Delete a mesh entity\n *\n * @param {EntityId} eId\n * @returns {boolean} - whether the api successfully deleted the meshEntity\n */\ndeleteMeshEntity(eId)\n```\n\n```ts\napi.deleteMeshEntity(boxId)\n```\n\n---\n\n## Throwables\n\nThrowables use the engine\'s built-in projectile system. Each throwable item has predefined velocity, damage, and gravity. You can multiply these defaults with the `velocityMult`, `damageMult`, and `gravityMult` parameters.\n\n### Creating a Throwable\n\n```ts\n/**\n * Try to create a throwable entity.\n * Similar to creating a mesh entity and uses the same rate limiting.\n * However, this uses the predefined throwables system and physics used by throwable items with the game\n * Each throwable item has its own behaviour already, including default velocity, damage and gravity multipliers.\n *\n * @param {EntityId} throwerEId\n * @param {ThrowableItem} itemName - Must be an Item that is usually throwable in-engine\n * @param {[number, number, number]} position - Starting position\n * @param {[number, number, number]} direction\n * @param {number} [velocityMult] - Multiplier for the default velocity of the throwable item\n * @param {number} [damageMult] - Multiplier for the default damage of the throwable item\n * @param {number} [gravityMult] - Multiplier for the default gravity of the throwable item\n * @param {ItemAttributes} [attributes] - item attributes (currently used only for the "Boomerag" item)\n * @returns {string} - null if throwable creation failed, otherwise the entity ID.\n */\nattemptCreateThrowable(throwerEId, itemName, position, direction, velocityMult, damageMult, gravityMult, attributes)\n```\n\n#### Example\n\n```ts\nconst pos = api.getPosition(playerId)\nconst { dir } = api.getPlayerFacingInfo(playerId)\nconst throwableId = api.attemptCreateThrowable(\n    playerId,\n    "Fireball",\n    [pos[0], pos[1] + 1.5, pos[2]],\n    dir,\n    2,    // double velocity\n    1.5,  // 1.5x damage\n)\n```\n\n### Deleting a Throwable\nSome throwables are deleted automatically when they hit a block or entity, or despawn after a certain time. You can delete them manually with this method.\n\n```ts\n/**\n * Delete a throwable entity before it automatically removes itself.\n *\n * @param {EntityId} eId\n * @returns {boolean} - true if the entity was deleted, false if it was not a throwable entity\n */\ndeleteThrowable(eId)\n```\n\n```ts\napi.deleteThrowable(throwableId)\n```\n\n---\n\n## Node Mesh Attachment\n\nAttach or detach a mesh to a specific node ("bone") of an entity. This is useful for attaching items, effects, or decorations to player body parts or other entity nodes.\n\n```ts\n/**\n * Attach/detach mesh instances to/from an entity\n *\n * @param {EntityId} eId\n * @param {EntityNamedNode} node - node to attach to\n * @param {MeshType | null} type - if null, detaches mesh from this node\n * @param {MeshEntityOpts[MeshType]} [opts]\n * @param {[number, number, number]} [offset]\n * @param {[number, number, number]} [rotation]\n * @returns {void}\n */\nupdateEntityNodeMeshAttachment(eId, node, type, opts, offset, rotation)\n```\n\n### Available Nodes\n\n`EntityNamedNode` is one of:\n\n- `"TorsoNode"`\n- `"HeadMesh"`\n- `"ArmRightMesh"`\n- `"ArmLeftMesh"`\n- `"LegLeftMesh"`\n- `"LegRightMesh"`\n\n### Examples\n\nAttach a block to a player\'s right arm:\n\n```ts\napi.updateEntityNodeMeshAttachment(\n    playerId,\n    "ArmRightMesh",\n    "BloxdBlock",\n    { blockName: "Block of Diamond", size: 0.3 },\n    [0, -0.5, 0],  // offset\n    [0, 0, 0],     // rotation\n)\n```\n\nAttach a glowing box to a player\'s head:\n\n```ts\napi.updateEntityNodeMeshAttachment(\n    playerId,\n    "HeadMesh",\n    "Box",\n    { width: 0.3, height: 0.3, depth: 0.3, emissiveColor: [255, 215, 0] },\n    [0, 0.5, 0],\n)\n```\n\nDetach a mesh from a node:\n\n```ts\napi.updateEntityNodeMeshAttachment(playerId, "ArmRightMesh", null)\n```\n\n---\n\n## Types Glossary\n\nReference types that you may find useful.\n\n### `MeshEntityOpts`\n\n```ts\ntype MeshEntityOpts = {\n    Box: CommonMeshEntityOpts & {\n        width: number\n        height: number\n        depth: number\n        diffuseColor?: number[]\n        emissiveColor?: number[]\n        backFaceCulling?: boolean // Default true\n        texture?: string // Can be a blockname. Wraps every one block\n        faceUV?: number[][]\n        animateTexture?: boolean // If true, `texture` must be an animated block name (e.g. "Lava", "Red Portal") and the Box cycles through its frames.\n    }\n    BloxdBlock: CommonMeshEntityOpts & {\n        blockName: BlockNameOrId\n        size: number | [number, number, number]\n        /** Enchantment sheen, drawn only when attached to an entity node, as a worn glider is. */\n        enchantmentTier?: EnchantmentTier\n    }\n    Person: CommonMeshEntityOpts & {\n        size?: number\n        textures?: Partial<Cosmetics>\n        pose?: PlayerPose\n    }\n    Leaderboard: LeaderboardMeshOpts\n    ParticleEmitter: MeshParticleSystemOpts\n}\n```\n\n### `CommonMeshEntityOpts`\n\n```ts\ntype CommonMeshEntityOpts = {\n    hideDist?: number\n    meshOffset?: number[]\n    autoRotate?: boolean\n    lineToEId?: EntityId // EntityId to connect to using a line\n}\n```\n\n### `MeshEntityPhysicsOpts`\n\n```ts\ntype MeshEntityPhysicsOpts = {\n    doPhysics: boolean\n    onCollideTerrain?: () => void // Unsupported for custom code\n    collidesEntities?: boolean\n    collideBits?: number // bitmask category of this entity\n    collideMask?: number // bitmask category of entities this entity collides with\n    heightExpandAmt?: number // expand hitbox height by this amount\n    widthExpandAmt?: number // expand hitbox width by this amount\n}\n```\n\n### `MeshParticleSystemOpts`\n\n```ts\ntype MeshParticleSystemOpts = ParticleSystemOpts &\n    CommonMeshEntityOpts & {\n        height: number\n        width: number\n        depth: number\n        emitRate: number\n        /** Include the followed lifeform\'s visual offset, including its vehicle seat. */\n        followTargetMeshOffset?: boolean\n        /** Ring emits radially from the perimeter; width/depth set its diameters, height its thickness. */\n        emitterShape?: "box" | "ring"\n        dir1?: number[]\n        dir2?: number[]\n    }\n```\n\n### `ParticleSystemOpts`\n\n```ts\ntype ParticleSystemOpts = {\n    texture: string\n    minLifeTime: number\n    maxLifeTime: number\n    minEmitPower: number\n    maxEmitPower: number\n    minSize: number\n    maxSize: number\n    gravity: number[]\n    velocityGradients: VelocityGradient[]\n    colorGradients: TimeColorGradient[] | RandomColorGradient[]\n    blendMode: ParticleSystemBlendMode\n}\n```\n\n### `TimeColorGradient`\n\nColours are [r, g, b, a]: RGB 0-255, alpha 0-1.\n\n```ts\ntype TimeColorGradient = {\n    timeFraction: number\n    minColor: [number, number, number, number]\n    maxColor?: [number, number, number, number]\n}\n```\n\n### `RandomColorGradient`\n\nColour is [r, g, b]: RGB 0-255.\n\n```ts\ntype RandomColorGradient = {\n    color: [number, number, number]\n}\n```\n\n### `VelocityGradient`\n\n```ts\ntype VelocityGradient = {\n    timeFraction: number\n    factor: number\n    factor2: number\n}\n```\n\n### `ParticleSystemBlendMode`\n\n```ts\nenum ParticleSystemBlendMode {\n    // Source color is added to the destination color without alpha affecting the result\n    OneOne = 0,\n    // Blend current color and particle color using particle\'s alpha\n    Standard = 1,\n    // Add current color and particle color multiplied by particle\'s alpha\n    Add,\n    // Multiply current color with particle color\n    Multiply,\n    // Multiply current color with particle color then add current color and particle color multiplied by particle\'s alpha\n    MultiplyAdd,\n}\n```\n\n### `EntityNamedNode`\n\nNodes on a player/entity skeleton that meshes can be attached to.\n\n```ts\ntype EntityNamedNode = "TorsoNode" | "HeadMesh" | "ArmRightMesh" | "ArmLeftMesh" | "LegLeftMesh" | "LegRightMesh"\n```\n'

+      id: "qte",
+      title: "QTEs",
+      content: '# Quick Time Events (QTEs)\n\nQTEs are interactive prompts shown to a player that require a response (clicking, holding, etc). They are triggered from server-side game code via `api.addQTE()` and the result is received via the `onPlayerFinishQTE` callback.\n\n## Overview\n\n- **`progressBar`**: Click rapidly to fill a progress bar before it drains to zero.\n- **`timedClick`**: Click within a time window to succeed.\n- **`gravityBar`**: Hold click to keep a catch zone aligned with a moving target.\n- **`precisionBar`**: Click when the marker is within the success zone to succeed.\n- **`rhythmClick`**: Click when a shrinking outer circle aligns with a fixed inner circle.\n\n## `progressBar`\n\nThe player clicks repeatedly to increase a progress bar. The bar drains continuously over time. Reaching 100% completes the QTE successfully. If `canFail` is true and progress reaches 0, the QTE fails; otherwise progress is clamped at 0 and the player can keep trying.\n\n### Parameters\n\n```ts\ntype ProgressBarQteParams = {\n    progressStartValue?: number // Starting progress value (0-100). default: 30\n    progressDecreasePerTick: number // How much progress drains each tick while the player isn\'t clicking. default: 0.075\n    progressPerClick: number // How much progress is gained per click. default: 5\n    canFail: boolean // If true, the QTE fails when progress reaches 0; otherwise progress clamps at 0. default: false\n    description: CustomTextStyling // Rich text shown as the QTE prompt. default: [{ str: "Click repeatedly to complete!" }]\n    clickIcon: string // Icon displayed on the click target. default: "fa-solid fa-computer-mouse"\n    scale?: number // Scale multiplier for the click icon (must be > 0). default: 1\n    rotation?: number // Rotation in degrees for the click icon (must be \u2265 0). default: 15\n}\n```\n\n### Sensible Defaults\n\n```ts\napi.addQTE(playerId, {\n    type: "progressBar",\n    parameters: {\n        progressStartValue: 30,\n        progressDecreasePerTick: 0.075,\n        progressPerClick: 5,\n        canFail: false,\n        description: [{ str: "Click repeatedly to complete!" }],\n        clickIcon: "fa-solid fa-computer-mouse",\n        scale: 3,\n        rotation: 15,\n    },\n})\n```\n\n## `timedClick`\n\nA prompt appears and the player must click before the timer runs out. Clicking within the time window succeeds; letting it expire fails the QTE.\n\n### Parameters\n\n```ts\ntype TimedClickQteParams = {\n    timeWindow: number // Duration in milliseconds the player has to click. default: 3000\n    icon: string // Icon displayed on the click target. default: "fa-solid fa-computer-mouse"\n    label: CustomTextStyling // Rich text shown as the QTE prompt. default: [{ str: "Click to complete the QTE!" }]\n    showTimer: boolean // Whether to display a countdown timer. default: true\n    scale?: number // Scale multiplier for the icon (must be > 0). default: 1\n    rotation?: number // Rotation in degrees for the icon (must be \u2265 0). default: 15\n    breatheCenter?: boolean // If true, the icon pulses with a breathing animation anchored to the centre. default: false\n}\n```\n\n### Sensible Defaults\n\n```ts\napi.addQTE(playerId, {\n    type: "timedClick",\n    parameters: {\n        timeWindow: 3000,\n        icon: "fa-solid fa-computer-mouse",\n        label: [{ str: "Click to complete the QTE!" }],\n        showTimer: true,\n        scale: 3,\n        rotation: 15,\n        breatheCenter: false,\n    },\n})\n```\n\n## `gravityBar`\n\nA mover travels along a bar, periodically changing direction. The player holds click to push their catch zone upward and releases to let gravity pull it down. Progress fills while the mover overlaps the catch zone and drains when it doesn\'t. Reaching 100% succeeds. If `canFail` is true, hitting 0% fails the QTE.\n\n### Parameters\n\n```ts\ntype GravityBarQteParams = {\n    progressStartValue?: number // Starting progress value (0-100). default: 30\n    catchZoneSize: number // Size of the player\'s catch zone as a fraction of the bar (must be > 0, 0-1). default: 0.25\n    moverSpeed: number // Speed at which the mover travels along the bar (must be > 0). default: 3\n    moverErraticness: number // How erratically the mover changes direction (higher = more unpredictable). default: 0.8\n    gravity: number // Downward pull on the catch zone when the player isn\'t holding click. default: 1\n    riseSpeed: number // Upward force on the catch zone while the player holds click. default: 1.5\n    progressGainPerSecond: number // Progress gained per second while the mover is inside the catch zone. default: 8\n    progressDrainPerSecond: number // Progress lost per second while the mover is outside the catch zone. default: 4\n    canFail: boolean // If true, the QTE fails when progress reaches 0; otherwise progress clamps at 0. default: false\n    description: CustomTextStyling // Rich text shown as the QTE prompt. default: [{ str: "Hold to catch!" }]\n    icon?: string // Icon displayed on the mover. default: "Moonfish"\n}\n```\n\n### Sensible Defaults\n\n```ts\napi.addQTE(playerId, {\n    type: "gravityBar",\n    parameters: {\n        progressStartValue: 30,\n        catchZoneSize: 0.25,\n        moverSpeed: 3,\n        moverErraticness: 0.8,\n        gravity: 1,\n        riseSpeed: 1.5,\n        progressGainPerSecond: 8,\n        progressDrainPerSecond: 4,\n        canFail: false,\n        description: [{ str: "Hold to catch!" }],\n        icon: "Moonfish",\n    },\n})\n```\n\n## `precisionBar`\n\nA marker oscillates back and forth along a bar. A highlighted success zone sits in the centre. The player has one click \u2014 if the marker is inside the success zone, the QTE succeeds; otherwise it fails. The marker keeps bouncing indefinitely until the player clicks.\n\n### Parameters\n\n```ts\ntype PrecisionBarQteParams = {\n    speed: number // Speed of the marker in full bar-widths per second (must be > 0, e.g. 1.0 = one full sweep per second). default: 0.5\n    successZoneSize: number // Fraction of the bar that counts as the success zone, centred in the middle (must be > 0, 0-1, e.g. 0.15 = 15%). default: 0.15\n    label: CustomTextStyling // Rich text shown as the QTE prompt. default: [{ str: "Click when the marker is within the green zone." }]\n    icon?: string // Icon displayed on the marker. default: ""\n    scale?: number // Scale multiplier for the icon (must be > 0). default: 1\n    rotation?: number // Rotation in degrees for the icon (must be \u2265 0). default: 0\n}\n```\n\n### Sensible Defaults\n\n```ts\napi.addQTE(playerId, {\n    type: "precisionBar",\n    parameters: {\n        speed: 0.5,\n        successZoneSize: 0.15,\n        label: [{ str: "Click when the marker is within the green zone." }],\n        icon: "",\n        scale: 1,\n        rotation: 0,\n    },\n})\n```\n\n## `rhythmClick`\n\nAn outer circle shrinks toward a fixed inner circle. The player must click when the two overlap. Each successful click counts toward `requiredSuccesses`. Missing the window (clicking too early/late or letting the circle pass without clicking) counts as a miss. If `maxMisses` is set and exceeded, the QTE fails; otherwise missed attempts simply reset the circle for another try.\n\n### Parameters\n\n```ts\ntype RhythmClickQteParams = {\n    requiredSuccesses: number // Number of successful clicks needed to complete the QTE (must be a positive integer). default: 5\n    shrinkDurationMs: number // Duration in milliseconds for the outer circle to shrink from max size to centre (must be > 0). default: 1200\n    toleranceFraction: number // Fraction of the inner circle radius that counts as a successful overlap (must be > 0, 0-1, e.g. 0.15 = \xb115%). default: 0.15\n    maxMisses?: number // Max misses allowed before failing. If omitted, unlimited misses are permitted (must be a non-negative integer). default: 3\n    label: CustomTextStyling // Rich text shown as the QTE prompt. default: [{ str: "Click when the circles align!" }]\n    icon?: string // Icon displayed in the centre of the circles. default: ""\n}\n```\n\n### Sensible Defaults\n\n```ts\napi.addQTE(playerId, {\n    type: "rhythmClick",\n    parameters: {\n        requiredSuccesses: 5,\n        shrinkDurationMs: 1200,\n        toleranceFraction: 0.15,\n        maxMisses: 3,\n        label: [{ str: "Click when the circles align!" }],\n        icon: "",\n    },\n})\n```\n\n## Usage\n\n### Starting a QTE\n\n```ts\nconst qteId = api.addQTE(playerId, {\n    type: "progressBar",\n    parameters: {\n        progressDecreasePerTick: 0.075,\n        progressPerClick: 7,\n        canFail: false,\n        description: [{ str: "Click repeatedly to complete!" }],\n        clickIcon: "fa-solid fa-computer-mouse",\n    },\n})\n```\n\n### Handling the Result\n\n```ts\nonPlayerFinishQTE(playerId, qteId, result) {\n    if (result) {\n        // Player succeeded\n    } else {\n        // Player failed\n    }\n}\n```\n\n### Cancelling a QTE\n\n```ts\napi.deleteQTE(playerId, qteId)\n```\n\n### Checking Active QTEs\n\n```ts\nconst hasQTE = api.hasActiveQTE(playerId)\n```\n'
